name: job-posting
purpose: The body of a careers posting page, under the posting's title band: the description in rows, one per section of the posting (a heading, then its paragraphs and bullet lists), beside a sticky rail that restates the posting (its area, its title and its facets such as department, location and contract) with the link to the application; then the application form, and a dialog that confirms a sent application with a way back to the open positions. From the design sample's careers job page. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'job-posting', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `section-module`, `frame-box`, `section-title`, `overline`, `button`, `field`, `label`, `input`, `phone-input`, `file-dropzone`, `file-token-group`, `alert`, `dialog` and `panel`. It collects data, so it follows the forms exception of the page-section contract: it validates on submit only and emits `submit`; the site sends the application and hands the outcome back through `loading`, `submitted` and `failed`.
useWhen: On the page of one open position, under a `hero-band` (`kind: 'title-band'`) that carries the posting's title and its apply link.
avoidWhen: For the list of open positions → use `listing-browser`.
For a lead or contact form at the top of a landing page → use `hero-form`.
For a newsletter sign-up at the end of a page → use `closing-call-to-action-newsletter`.
related: hero-band` — the title band above the posting; its action links to `#` plus `form.anchor`.
hero-form` — the sibling page section that also emits `submit` and takes `loading`, `submitted` and `failed`.
bestPractices: Write each section as a short heading and its `blocks`: a `text` block per paragraph, a `list` block per bullet list, in the posting's order.
Keep `facets` to the four the listing states (department, location, work arrangement, contract), each with a glyph.
Set `form.anchor` (for example `apply`) and point the title band's action at `#apply`; the rail's apply button links there too.
Put the format and size limits of a `file` field in its `helper`, and the accepted types in `accept`.
Mark only what the team needs as `required`; say "Optional." in the `helper` of the rest.
Send the application from the `submit` handler, read the file from `new FormData(event.target)`, and set `loading`, then `submitted` or `failed`.

props.name: form
props.doc: The application form: `{ title, description?, submitLabel, anchor?, ariaLabel?, fields }`, where `anchor` is the id of the apply section the rail button links to and a field is `{ name, kind, label, required?, helper?, placeholder?, accept?, autocomplete?, country? }`.

props.name: messages
props.doc: Copy of the form and its outcomes: `{ missing, invalidEmail, invalidUrl, error, successTitle, successDescription, done, browse }`.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the band so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: area
props.doc: Area the posting is filed under, the overline of the rail.

props.name: title
props.doc: Title of the posting, restated at the top of the rail; the band renders nothing when empty.

props.name: facets
props.doc: Facts about the posting listed in the rail, in order; each is `{ label, icon? }`.

props.name: applyLabel
props.doc: Label of the rail button that links to the application form; the button is left out when empty.

props.name: sections
props.doc: The description, one row per section in order; each is `{ title, blocks }` where a block is `{ kind: 'text', text }` or `{ kind: 'list', items }`.

props.name: secondaryAction
props.doc: Link in the confirmation dialog back to the open positions; `{ label, href }`. Omitted when absent.

props.name: loading
props.doc: The site is sending the application: the submit button shows its loading state, every control is disabled and a submit is ignored.

props.name: submitted
props.doc: The site sent the application: the confirmation dialog opens.

props.name: failed
props.doc: The site could not send the application: `messages.error` shows under the submit button.

examples.name: Default
examples.sfc:
<script setup>
  import JobPosting from '@aziontech/webkit/job-posting'
  import { nextTick, ref } from 'vue'

  const facets = [
    {
      label: 'Engineering',
      icon: 'ai ai-sitemap'
    },
    {
      label: 'San Francisco, California',
      icon: 'ai ai-map-pin'
    },
    {
      label: 'Hybrid',
      icon: 'ai ai-building'
    },
    {
      label: 'Full-time',
      icon: 'ai ai-clock'
    }
  ]

  const sections = [
    {
      title: 'About Acme',
      blocks: [
        {
          kind: 'text',
          text: 'Acme builds the platform teams use to ship and run their applications worldwide. We are a small team with a big footprint, and we care about tools that get out of the way.'
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      title: 'About the role',
      blocks: [
        {
          kind: 'text',
          text: 'As a Senior Platform Engineer you will turn quality into a built-in capability of our engineering platform: automation, internal tools and standards that remove manual steps from the delivery cycle.'
        },
        {
          kind: 'text',
          text: 'You will work with the development, platform and infrastructure teams on self-service tools, standard pipelines and automated release checks.'
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      title: 'What you will do',
      blocks: [
        {
          kind: 'list',
          items: [
            'Build and evolve standard CI/CD pipelines for tests, checks and releases.',
            'Write internal frameworks and tools for test automation.',
            'Automate functional, integration and end-to-end tests.',
            'Guide engineers in testing and automation practices.'
          ]
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      title: 'What you bring',
      blocks: [
        {
          kind: 'list',
          items: [
            'Experience with test automation and quality engineering.',
            'Solid experience with CI/CD and pipeline automation.',
            'Tooling written in TypeScript, Python or Go.',
            'Working knowledge of Linux and containers.'
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]

  const form = {
    anchor: 'apply',
    title: 'Do you want to build with us?',
    description: 'Fill in the form to apply for this position.',
    submitLabel: 'Submit application',
    fields: [
      {
        name: 'name',
        kind: 'text',
        label: 'Name',
        required: true,
        autocomplete: 'name'
      },
      {
        name: 'email',
        kind: 'email',
        label: 'Email address',
        required: true,
        helper: 'We answer every application at this address.'
      },
      {
        name: 'phone',
        kind: 'phone',
        label: 'Contact number',
        required: true
      },
      {
        name: 'linkedin',
        kind: 'url',
        label: 'LinkedIn profile URL',
        helper: 'Optional.'
      },
      {
        name: 'resume',
        kind: 'file',
        label: 'Resume',
        required: true,
        accept: 'application/pdf,.docx,.doc',
        helper: '.pdf, .docx or .doc, up to 5 MB'
      }
    ]
  }

  const messages = {
    missing: 'This field is required.',
    invalidEmail: 'Enter an email address like name@example.com.',
    invalidUrl: 'Enter the full URL, starting with https://.',
    error: 'We could not send your application. Try again in a few minutes.',
    successTitle: 'Application sent',
    successDescription:
      'Thank you for applying. We read every application and will reply by email.',
    done: 'Done',
    browse: 'Browse files'
  }

  const submitted = ref(false)

  const send = async () => {
    submitted.value = false
    await nextTick()
    submitted.value = true
  }
</script>

<template>
  <JobPosting
    area="Engineering"
    title="Senior Platform Engineer"
    apply-label="Apply for this position"
    :facets="facets"
    :sections="sections"
    :form="form"
    :messages="messages"
    :secondary-action="{ label: 'See open positions', href: '/careers' }"
    :submitted="submitted"
    @submit="send"
  />
</template>
